newsitem.title: USA: Tornado hits near downtown Miami.
newsitem.headline: Tornado hits near downtown Miami.

text.p: A tornado swept through Miami on Monday, uprooting trees, sweeping a cloud of debris into the air and narrowly missing the city's busy downtown business district.
The spectacular funnel cloud moved across the northern edge of downtown Miami and into Biscayne Bay, tracking close to the Venetian and MacArthur causeways, roadways linking Miami to Miami Beach.
Local media reports said trees were uprooted and tossed around by the tornado, but there were no immediate reports of serious damage or injuries.
The storm touched down right next to the Miami Police Department headquarters.

"It went right next to our station. We have trees that have fallen on top of employee's cars, a light pole fell on a car. We're just trying to cope with the damage to our facility," said Liz Babun-Matos, a worker at the police station.

The storm narrowly missed the city's downtown core where the major businesses are located. Stunned office workers ran to their windows to watch the spinning cloud, which carried hundreds of pieces of debris in its spiral as it swept through the city.
